extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Peer Community In (PCI) Registered Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer review of Registered Reports submitted to PCI, covering Stage 1 (proposed protocol) and Stage 2 (completed study) evaluations, required checks, recommended decisions, and how to phrase constructive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question / importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission address an important, clearly stated research question or hypothesis that is of interest to the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Stage 1 focus on whether the question is theoretically or practically meaningful and whether justifying literature is cited; do not penalize results (Stage 2) — assess importance independent of outcome. Antipatterns: vague or multiple competing questions, lack of rationale for why the question matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and theoretical framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the theoretical background/literature review sufficient, accurate, and targeted to motivate the hypotheses or research aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that prior work is cited, competing theories acknowledged, and that the logic linking prior evidence to the present hypotheses is explicit. Guidance includes identifying missing key references or mistaken interpretations of cited studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and specificity of hypotheses / predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are hypotheses or research predictions stated clearly and unambiguously, with directionality and expected effects specified where appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For confirmatory analyses, hypotheses should be precise (e.g., specifying expected relationships, contrasts). Ambiguous or post-hoc phrasing should be flagged. Recommend distinguishing primary and secondary hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between confirmatory and exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the protocol clearly separate confirmatory (pre-registered) analyses from exploratory/unplanned analyses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that planned confirmatory tests are explicitly identified and that any planned exploratory analyses are labeled as such. Advise authors to specify how exploratory findings will be interpreted and reported to avoid p-hacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design and methodological appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the overall design (experimental/quasi-experimental/observational) appropriate to answer the research question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess control conditions, counterbalancing, manipulations, observational measures, and whether the design allows causal inference where claimed. Flag design choices that undermine interpretability (e.g., lack of controls for obvious confounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization and measurement validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the constructs operationalized with valid, reliable measures, and are procedures described in sufficient detail?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for measurement validity evidence, details on instruments/surveys/tasks, and how scores are computed. Request sample items, coding manuals, or concrete descriptions when missing. Antipattern: vague descriptions like 'standard questionnaire' without citation or item list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification and statistical power
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the sample size justified (e.g., power analysis, precision-based justification, feasibility) and adequate for the planned primary analyses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit power calculations or other transparent justifications (e.g., minimal detectable effect, precision goals) including assumptions (effect size, alpha, model). Flag underpowered designs and unclear justifications; suggest alternative approaches (sequential designs, Bayesian planning) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the analysis plan fully specified for primary confirmatory tests, including models, covariates, transformations, handling of outliers, and decision rules?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect clear specification of statistical models, variables, contrasts, alpha levels, multiple comparison corrections, and any planned subgroup analyses. Anti-patterns: 'we will analyze as appropriate' or leaving model selection to data-driven choices without rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions, diagnostics and robustness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the plan include checks of statistical assumptions and pre-specified robustness/sensitivity analyses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require articulation of key assumptions (e.g., normality, independence), how they will be assessed, and alternative analyses if assumptions fail. Recommend pre-specified robustness checks and inclusion of alternative modeling approaches where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization and allocation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Are randomization and allocation procedures for experimental assignments clearly described and adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check details of randomization mechanism, stratification/blocking, allocation concealment, and how randomization will be implemented and recorded. Flag inadequate or absent randomization procedures in experimental designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding / masking procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Are blinding or masking procedures for participants, experimenters, and/or outcome assessors described and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether blinding is necessary and feasible, how it will be implemented, and how failures of blinding will be handled. If blinding is not possible, request justification and alternative safeguards against bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria and participant flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Are eligibility criteria, recruitment plans, and rules for excluding participants (including preregistered data exclusion rules) clearly specified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect concrete inclusion/exclusion rules, recruitment targets, anticipated attrition, and pre-specified criteria for excluding data (e.g., attention check failures). Check that planned CONSORT-like flow reporting is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping rules and interim analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Are stopping rules and any planned interim analyses (and their statistical control) pre-specified and justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For designs with potential interim looks, require explicit stopping criteria, alpha spending or Bayesian decision rules, and how type I error is controlled. Antipatterns: vague statements about 'checking data periodically' without rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility, timeline and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed plan feasible given the stated timeline, resources, and team expertise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether recruitment rates, equipment, labs, and personnel make the project realistic. Flag unrealistic timelines, under-resourced procedures, or missing access to required samples or data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approvals and participant protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the submission addressed ethical considerations and plans for obtaining approvals (IRB/ethics), consent procedures, and data privacy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect mention of ethics approvals or plans to obtain them, consent processes, data anonymization, and handling of sensitive data. Recommend clarifications when ethical issues are overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials, code and data availability / open-science practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Are plans for sharing materials, analysis code, and data specified (timing, repositories, access conditions)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage pre-specified data/code sharing plans, use of persistent repositories, and any restrictions (e.g., sensitive data). For Stage 2, check that promised materials/code are deposited and accessible or that valid reasons for restrictions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and transparency of procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript sufficiently detailed for another competent team to reproduce the study or analyses from the protocol/materials/code?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for step-by-step procedural details, operational definitions, code for analyses, and sample materials. Request additions where procedures are underspecified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the plan specify how missing data will be handled and whether assumptions of missingness mechanisms will be assessed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require pre-specified methods (e.g., multiple imputation, full-information models), sensitivity analyses for missingness, and thresholds/triggers for data exclusion due to missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple comparisons and family-wise error control
rubrics_metrics.description: Are issues of multiple testing addressed and controlled for in the analysis plan?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect plans for correction (Bonferroni, FDR, pre-specifying primary outcomes) or justification for why corrections are not needed. Flag uncorrected multiple unplanned tests posing inflated false positive risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Fidelity to approved Stage 1 protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: For Stage 2 reviews, did the authors adhere to their approved Stage 1 protocol, and are deviations transparently reported and justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare executed methods and analyses with Stage 1; accept minor, justified deviations but require clear documentation and rationale for important changes. If deviations affect confirmatory status, require relabeling of affected analyses as exploratory or require re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Reporting of results and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Are results presented clearly, with appropriate summaries, effect sizes, uncertainty estimates, and interpretation consistent with the pre-specified hypotheses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that authors report exact test statistics, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and do not overinterpret non-significant or exploratory findings. Confirmatory conclusions should be supported by the pre-registered analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of exploratory analyses and post-hoc tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Are exploratory and post-hoc analyses clearly labeled and distinguished from confirmatory tests in the report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any post-hoc findings are explicitly identified as exploratory and not used to retroactively justify the primary hypothesis; suggest replication of exploratory findings in future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation proportional to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the discussion and conclusions remain proportionate to the strength of the evidence and acknowledge limitations and alternative explanations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag overreaching claims, causal language unsupported by design, and failure to discuss limitations, generalizability, or null results. Recommend tempering claims or adding qualifiers when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting clarity, organization and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript/protocol well organized, clearly written, and complete (figures, tables, preregistration links, supplementary materials included)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request clarifications for ambiguous phrasing, missing figures/tables, or absent links to preregistration, data, or code. Encourage readability and clear labeling of primary outcomes and tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical competence and appropriateness of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Are chosen statistical methods appropriate and competently applied for the data and hypotheses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether models match data structure (nested data, repeated measures), whether assumptions are met, and whether advanced methods are used correctly. Suggest simpler alternatives if methods appear misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct of reviewer (conflicts of interest and confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should declare conflicts of interest and respect the confidential nature of registered reports under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes recusing oneself when conflicts are present, not sharing confidential materials, and disclosing any potential COIs to the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation categories and decision guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear recommendation (e.g., Accept-in-Principle, Minor Revisions, Major Revisions, Reject) with justification tied to the criteria above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Stage 1, recommend in-principle acceptance when hypotheses, methods, and analyses are sound and feasible; otherwise indicate required revisions (minor/major) or rejection. For Stage 2, recommend final acceptance if fidelity and reporting are adequate, or require revisions. Explain that reviewers should focus on methodological rigor, not desirability of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive tone and actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be constructive, specific, and actionable to help authors improve their protocol/manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific suggestions (e.g., 'specify covariates X and Y', 'provide power calculation with effect size rationale'), avoid vague criticisms, and explain why changes are necessary. When requesting additional analyses, specify precisely what is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior publication and overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission appropriately discloses prior dissemination, preprints, or overlapping data/analyses and whether this affects novelty or evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request clarity and justification when parts of the work are already public; advise editors if overlap undermines the novelty or registered-report desirability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks for questionable research practices and p-hacking risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate risks of undisclosed flexibility in data collection or analysis that could lead to biased results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for vague decision rules, many undisclosed analytic choices, or incentives for stopping studies early; recommend pre-specifying analytic decision trees and documenting all degrees of freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about deviations, post-approval changes and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Are procedures in place to document and justify any amendments to the Stage 1 plan (e.g., protocol changes) and are such amendments transparent in the Stage 2 report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Stage 2, require a clear amendments table or section explaining when, why, and how protocol changes occurred and whether they were approved by the handling editor.
